text: CAN/ASC – EN 301 549:2024. The 2024 announcement describes voluntary use.

ABNT NBR 17225:2025 covers web accessibility based on WCAG 2.2. Section 6 links EN 301 549 V3.2.1 as supporting material; bibliography item 11 links V2.1.2. These references alone do not establish adoption of EN 301 549.
Commission WAD guidance lists V3.2.1. The ETSI schedule records V4.1.1 publication and a target for OJ citation; its achieved citation date is blank. The target is not confirmation of citation.
KENYA STANDARD KS 2952-1:2022, ICS 33.030; 53.080, First Edition
NMX-R-099-SCFI-2018: official catalogue; previously listed PDF (not rechecked). ICT accessibility requirements for public procurement in Mexico. EN edition/equivalence remains under review.
Draft Digital Accessibility Standard. Final version expected early 2027; start date and mandated agencies remain unconfirmed.

questions.Australia: Resolved the prior current-catalogue question: AS EN 301 549:2024 supersedes the 2020 edition. Preserve the 2020 sample and version as history. Follow-up: inspect future catalogue amendments; establish legal/procurement obligations separately if needed.
questions.Japan: Resolved cited-document type: CPR-6201 is a technical report with a translation annex. This correction concerns the cited document, not a claim that no Japanese adoption exists elsewhere. Follow-up: a national standards-body record is needed for a broader adoption claim.
questions.India: Resolved technical relationship in the BIS foreword. Follow-up: prefer a BIS-hosted accessible copy and independently research any mandatory scope only if required; do not infer it from publication.
questions.United Kingdom: Resolved publication and supersession using BSI. Exact EN 301 549:2021 designation used instead of inferring a version string from an internal identifier. Follow-up: catalogue amendments and legal use remain separate checks.
questions.Mexico: Resolved EN edition and modified relationship from the standard preface. Catalogue equivalence fields conflict; preface is the basis for the public wording. Preserve prior uncertainty and source history. Follow-up: check amendments and compulsory-use claims separately.
questions.Norway: The inherited 2025-06-28 date is still unsupported. Public row now describes the evidenced WAD reference and dates only the 12 additional WCAG criteria/accessibility-statement requirement. National standards adoption remains a separate unresolved question. Monitoring handoff: inspect the authority guidance on public-sector statement duties; register a monitoring domain/destination before a public addition (no monitoring domain currently exists).
questions.European Union: Resolved access to the historical 2021 WAD OJ decision and confirmed its citation date. Continue to check directive-specific current OJ acts for V4.1.1; no completed EAA citation established by the ETSI target. Prior failed-access attempts retained.
questions.Canada: Official standard identity and publication month rechecked; announcement date/voluntary use remain supported by the earlier record, not a fresh full review. Follow-up: assess amendments or legal use separately.
questions.Brazil: Partial PDF recheck only. Bibliography found; encoded section 6 hyperlink not independently resolved in this round. Earlier verified source-fidelity evidence retained. Follow-up remains whether another instrument establishes adoption or legal use.
questions.New Zealand: Draft and provisional reference unchanged. Follow up on final publication, start date, issuing authority and mandated agencies. Monitoring handoff: sections 3.5 and 4.4 propose statements, monitoring/reporting and GCDO testing; no monitoring domain exists, so register scope and verify final text before publishing.
questions.Kenya: Both reader and one ordinary-browser attempt left the linked PDF unreadable. Follow-up: locate an accessible ICT Authority or KEBS copy of KS 2952-1:2022 and inspect the foreword, edition relationship and status; do not infer from filename.
questions.Iceland: No inspectable ÍST catalogue source located; inherited adoption unchanged. Next useful action: locate a precise national identifier/catalogue entry or supplied primary evidence, not repeated generic searches.
questions.Switzerland: eCH source supports WCAG guidance but does not settle the inherited EN reference. Next useful action: obtain a precise SNV catalogue identifier or official instrument explicitly referencing EN 301 549.
questions.Turkey: Government platform statement is only a scoped lead. Next useful action: obtain a TSE catalogue record with TS identifier, EN edition and adoption/publication date.
